cognitive_frame: Product requirement clarity grounded in decision traceability and user value: frames every question as whether a reader knows what to build, for whom, within what boundaries, and how to observe success — without implementation detail — with scope clarity and observable acceptance as part of the genre mission.

expression_conventions.register: user- and outcome-oriented prose in each section intent; lead with who/what/why before how; forbid marketing and implementation register; prefer before→after outcome contrast at the product level when facts support it
expression_conventions.carriers: follow Derive F/C from section-form-registry; prefer bullet lists for capabilities and acceptance checks; one concrete scenario example where scenario intent applies (or explicit N/A); one-line empty/failure note on flows when relevant; no architecture diagrams or code-level steps
expression_conventions.scannability: short items over walls; comparable claims in tables; contrast partitions only when facts already contain the contrast; do not mix goals, scope, and acceptance in one dense paragraph; present those concerns in separate leaves or blocks rather than one undifferentiated surface
expression_conventions.altitude: product requirements only — observable acceptance; no file paths, APIs, or stack choices

intent_anchor: decision-doc remains SSOT for scope and boundaries; product-spec states what and why, not how to implement; technical feasibility and architecture belong to downstream technical stages — flag product-level assumptions only when they affect scope or acceptance
audience_type: primary: product owner and stakeholders confirming scope; secondary: downstream technical readers who need unambiguous requirements — after a clear through-line, a reader can state what is in/out of scope and how to verify done, or point to section-level gaps
